subject: Staggered overlap for technical deep dive — Tangent AI / ACME architects
messages:
From: Anna Kwan <anna.kwan@tangent.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: acme.techlead@acme-industries.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: technical deep dive to align infra + network (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — our platform team and network architects would like a focused technical deep dive to align on deployment topology, VPC peering patterns, and latency expectations.

We have architects in three regions (US East, Frankfurt, Singapore) so the challenge is finding a practical time to get the right people in the room. We were hoping Redwood could propose a scheduling approach that minimizes the number of duplicate sessions while keeping each meeting < 90 minutes.

What would help from your side:
- A couple of overlap strategies (single long session vs staggered short sessions) with concrete UTC times we can assess.
- A tentative agenda (focus areas + owners).
- Your recommended SEs to run the technical portions for each region.

We have a few constraints to flag: ACME architects prefer to avoid late evenings local time, and Tangent’s lead architect (Singapore) has limited windows between 08:00–11:00 SGT. Also worth noting: we have DST shifts in EU/US later in Q4 — any plan should be easy to replicate after those changes.

Thanks,
Anna Kwan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Tangent AI

Attachment: constraints-summary.txt (text)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Kwan <anna.kwan@tangent.ai>
Cc: acme.techlead@acme-industries.com, tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 12:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: technical deep dive to align infra + network (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear constraints, this is exactly the info we need.

High level suggestion: staggered overlap windows — two shorter, focused sessions (45–60 min each) timed so each includes one customer architect group and one Redwood SE. That keeps sessions technical and avoids forcing any attendee into the middle of the night.

Proposed options (all times in UTC for clarity):

Option A — Single longer overlap (90 min)
- Fri 2026-09-03 14:00–15:30 UTC (works for EU afternoon, US morning; Singapore will be late night)

Option B — Staggered overlap (recommended)
- Session 1: Thu 2026-09-02 14:00–14:45 UTC (US morning / EU afternoon)
- Session 2: Fri 2026-09-03 02:00–02:45 UTC (EU evening / APAC morning — less convenient for US)

Option C — Mirror short sessions across regions (if you want complete local comfort)
- Session US/EU: Thu 2026-09-02 15:00–15:45 UTC
- Session EU/APAC: Fri 2026-09-03 01:00–01:45 UTC

Notes:
- I attached a proposed-time-matrix.xlsx with conversions for EST/CET/SGT and an initial agenda.
- We recommend two SEs: Marcus Lin to lead the APAC-friendly session and Tessa Morgan to lead the US/EU session. Aditya can cover networking specifics and succeed as backup for either session.

Quick ask: please flag which option you prefer and which of the two sessions must include your Singapore architect (so we make sure to prioritize that overlap).

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: proposed-time-matrix.xlsx, agenda-deep-dive.pdf

Team — quick internal coordination thread after I sent options to Tangent/ACME. Key points:
- Customer prefers to avoid late evenings for ACME (they're in Frankfurt / CET). Tangent has Singapore constraints for mornings.
- I recommended Option B (staggered overlap) as the least disruptive.

Can you each confirm availability for the proposed slots?
- Session 1 (Thu 2026-09-02 14:00–14:45 UTC): Tessa lead + Aditya (networking)
- Session 2 (Fri 2026-09-03 02:00–02:45 UTC): Marcus lead + Aditya (backup)

Also a note on DST: EU/US offsets change in Q4. If Tangent wants recurring sessions or an extended program, we should adopt UTC anchors (we can re-run the matrix).

Replies: yes/no + any needed swap. I can cover escalation if the Singapore engineer needs a different slot.
